trust_decision.summary: The 24-bit wire AVP Length is trusted to cover the AVP's own header, but the only guard compares it against the 8-byte non-vendor header while the Vendor flag makes the header 12 bytes, so Length 8..11 underflows uint32 and make([]byte, dataLength) requests ~4 GiB; the decision is made in decodeDiameterAVP, and both exported routes into it converge there.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the Diameter AVP decoder and a header-size underflow; the only subtraction of a header size from a wire length in the tree is here, immediately before the attacker-sized make(), reachable as soon as the Vendor flag is set.

fix_sites.entry_point: (*Diameter).DecodeFromBytes (public, gopacket.DecodingLayer; reached via gopacket.NewPacket(data, LayerTypeDiameter, ...) / DecodingLayerParser and via the port demux at layers/ports.go:82,155,216) and ParseDiameterAVPs (layers/diameter_avp_decoders.go:79)
fix_sites.module_kind: public API of the layers package (protocol decoder)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no O2 site and no O8 route: one guard in the shared helper covers both exported entry points; the only dismissal a solver has is that ParseDiameterAVPs is an exported helper with no in-tree caller and no test, so hardening the layer decoder alone looks sufficient.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Per-AVP failure is non-fatal and empty AVPs are legal: the AVP loop sets df.SetTruncated() and breaks while DecodeFromBytes still returns nil, and an AVP whose Length equals the header size (8 non-vendor, 12 vendor) carries zero data; an over-broad fix that returns a message-level error, or rejects Length <= headerSize instead of Length < headerSize, breaks valid decoding.

O6_input_shapes: Vendor flag set with 24-bit AVP Length 8..11, i.e. below the 12-byte vendor header (the shapes 0x08-0x0b covered by the new test)
the same vendor AVP nested inside a Grouped AVP, where the sub-AVP loop re-enters decodeDiameterAVP

O8b_injection_room.sibling: message-level twin of the same mechanism: a 24-bit MessageLength trusted against the fixed 20-byte message header, data[20:d.MessageLength] (and data[:d.MessageLength] at :167) with no MessageLength >= 20 guard
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The decoder already passes the truncation check at :131 for any MessageLength below 20 and then slices past it, so a maintainer hardening declared-length fields would plausibly guard the message header the same way they guard the AVP header.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an independent implementation of ParseDiameterAVPs that recomputes headerSize from the vendor flag itself instead of delegating to decodeDiameterAVP
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A fast-path AVP-set parser written to avoid the per-AVP function call would duplicate the header-size arithmetic and reproduce exactly the underflow the published fix closes.

O9_family: integer underflow (CWE-191) on a length field leading to unbounded allocation / resource exhaustion (CWE-770)

O10_build.toolchain: Go 1.24 (go.mod: go 1.24.0); the layers package needs no cgo, while a full ./... build needs libpcap-dev for pcap/pfring/afpacket
O10_build.project_tests: layers/diameter_test.go: TestDiameterDecoding, TestDiameterVendorAVP (:112), TestDiameterSerialization, TestDiameterGroupedAVP, TestDiameterHelperFunctions, TestDiameterVendorAVPTypes, TestDiameter3GPPVendorAVP (:428); none exercises a Length below the header size and none calls ParseDiameterAVPs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the length-vs-header check in the AVP loop of Diameter.DecodeFromBytes (the route a PoC exercises) instead of in the shared decodeDiameterAVP, leaving the exported ParseDiameterAVPs route open.

out_of_scope_notes: layers/diameter.go:154,167: a Diameter message whose 24-bit MessageLength is below 20 passes the truncation check at :131 and then panics on data[20:d.MessageLength]; recovered by NewPacket/DecodingLayerParser but not by a direct DecodeFromBytes call - a different sink from the AVP allocation, so not counted here.
